answer: In an agent marketplace, each account must lock a bond before it can bid, and completed work builds a nontransferable reputation that raises its future bidding weight. If a buyer proves several accounts share one controller, an arbitrator can slash their bonds and pay the challenger. Splitting one agent into many therefore does not multiply earned trust: the attacker must fund every bond, keep capital locked, and risk losing it. Even an inlet agent named onyx can leave an ember of reputation only by doing real work.
